bundles.spec:
[fork-baseline-version, 1.5 h] Already done by the setup stage, do not redo: mod_version=1.1.52-skytekx.1 with upstream's archivesName ActuallyAdditions-1.20.1 and no BUILD_NUMBER suffix, the reproducible jar (SHA-1 c37140ce60ec6da5ac33ebea66b3f9fa3951f7fd), LICENSE and NOTICE in the jar as LICENSE_actuallyadditions and NOTICE_actuallyadditions, and the mods.toml fields license, issueTrackerURL and credits (fork commits 9788dd82 and 6bcbeadd, UPSTREAM.md build changes 1 to 9). Remaining work: (1) mods.toml gets optional dependencies on patchouli (versionRange [1.20.1-81,)), curios ([5.0,)) and jei ([15.0,)), each mandatory=false, ordering NONE, side BOTH. Patchouli stays optional in mods.toml as upstream does (main's neoforge.mods.toml declares no Patchouli dependency, only the Modrinth publish block marks it required, build.gradle:287), and ItemBooklet warns in chat when it is missing (19cfbc92). (2) src/main/resources/pack.mcmeta still says pack_format 6 with a 1.16 comment (UPSTREAM.md gap list): set 15, the 1.20.1 resource and data pack format. (3) Delete src/main/java/invtweaks/ (two live annotation classes that end up in the jar as package invtweaks.api.container, unchecked license, and a second mod jar with the same package would fail Forge's module layer with a split package) together with the fully commented ContainerGiantChest that alone imports them, as 9bc38d2a does on 1.20.4. The fully commented util/crafting/RecipeHelper.java (header names a third party author and 'MIT License' without the notice text) may go in the same commit since it compiles to nothing. (4) Optional: exclude src/generated/resources/.cache from processResources so the 18 .cache entries leave the jar. (5) ThreadSpecialFetcher (client only, SpecialRenderInit) fetches specialPeopleStuff.properties from the dead 1.16 branch URL: point it at main's specialPeopleStuffNew.properties as d9b0a714 did, or leave it, it never runs on the server. The UpdateChecker stays dead (constructor body commented out, onTick carries @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT)). Every change gets its line in UPSTREAM.md 'Source changes' and the NOTICE summary.
Upstream commits: 33f55411 and 226a4391 (already in the snapshot), 717199ea (twin of 33f55411), 9bc38d2a, d9b0a714.
Files (on the base or new): src/main/resources/META-INF/mods.toml, src/main/resources/pack.mcmeta, src/main/java/invtweaks/, mod/inventory/ContainerGiantChest.java, build.gradle, UPSTREAM.md, NOTICE.
Translation: Version naming follows the task rule. Keep 1.1.52 as the base number: the code base is 1.1.52, and UPSTREAM.md and NOTICE state the content level as 'content parity: upstream 1.3.26 (cd9d9c63) except the exclusions'. A 1.3.26 base number would claim parity with a NeoForge 1.21.1 build that has data components and 1.21 content and would point bug reports at the wrong changelog. UPSTREAM.md already records 1.3.26-skytekx.N as the alternative for the release. Nothing in the pack depends on the mod version.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: compileJava and build. The jar has no invtweaks/ entries, two clean builds give the same SHA-1 (record it, the OLD jar of the savegame test is the one named in baseline-boot-smoke), the Forge mod list shows 1.1.52-skytekx.1, Forge checks the version range of Patchouli, Curios and JEI when they are present (the mod list of Forge 47 shows no dependencies), the resource pack screen shows no 'made for an older version' marker for the mod resources.

[build-integrations-and-mixins, 3 h] Add compileOnly fg.deobf for the full Patchouli jar vazkii.patchouli:Patchouli:1.20.1-85-FORGE (the pack ships 85, fall back to 84 if maven.blamejared.com lacks 85), not the api classifier: PageReconstructor extends vazkii.patchouli.client.book.page.abstr.PageSimpleProcessingRecipe and PatchouliPages uses vazkii.patchouli.client.book.ClientBookRegistry (main PatchouliPages.java:4, PageReconstructor.java:10-11), neither is API. Add compileOnly fg.deobf top.theillusivec4.curios:curios-forge:5.14.1+1.20.1:api from maven.theillusivec4.top plus runtimeOnly fg.deobf of the full Curios jar for dev runs. Keep JEI 15.3.0.4 api. Do not add PatchouliProvider: the book is hand written, see patchouli-booklet. Mixin: Forge 47 does not read [[mixins]] from mods.toml (that is the NeoForge form that main's neoforge.mods.toml uses). Register the config through the jar manifest attribute MixinConfigs: 'actuallyadditions.mixins.json', the way ports/enderio/build.gradle:342 and ports/spiced-twilight/build.gradle:125 do. Pin the plugin org.spongepowered.mixin 0.7.38 (as ports/littletiles and ports/skytekx-defixes), add annotationProcessor 'org.spongepowered:mixin:0.8.5:processor' and a mixin { add sourceSets.main, 'actuallyadditions.refmap.json' ; config 'actuallyadditions.mixins.json' } block. The config is main's file with compatibilityLevel JAVA_17 (main says JAVA_21), minVersion 0.8.5, required true, defaultRequire 1, refmap actuallyadditions.refmap.json, mixins AnvilMixin and ItemCombinerMenuAccessor, client client.MinecraftMixin. The mixin classes land with item-tag-filter and engineer-goggles, so this feature adds the config with empty lists or lands together with the first mixin.
Upstream commits: 654465b3, 84d5eb0a, 983cc048, a5563774, 9378ea39, 6f567725, 3b297993.
Files (on the base or new): build.gradle, gradle.properties, src/main/resources/actuallyadditions.mixins.json.
Translation: The 1.21 localRuntime and moddev blocks become FG6 compileOnly or runtimeOnly fg.deobf. Arclight: checked with javap on common.jar of arclight-forge-1.20.1-1.0.6-6de9fec-safeiter2: its RepairContainerMixin only redirects and injects inside AnvilMenu.createResult, and its ItemCombinerMixin does not touch inputSlots, so AnvilMixin (HEAD inject in AnvilMenu.mayPickup) and the inputSlots accessor do not collide. MinecraftMixin injects at HEAD of Minecraft.shouldEntityAppearGlowing, client only. No @Overwrite anywhere.

New ids: none.
Test: compileJava with the mixin annotation processor, the refmap and the MixinConfigs manifest entry are in the jar, two clean builds still give the same SHA-1, a dedicated Forge server and the Arclight pack boot load the config without 'Mixin apply failed'.

[port-patch-pipeline, 2 h] A scratchpad script (not committed) that exports one upstream commit as a patch limited to src/main/java, src/main/resources and the hand written data, rewrites the mechanical NeoForge names (net.neoforged.neoforge -> net.minecraftforge, NeoForge.EVENT_BUS -> MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS, ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath and withDefaultNamespace -> new ResourceLocation, DeferredHolder, DeferredItem and DeferredBlock -> RegistryObject, BuiltInRegistries.X in registration -> ForgeRegistries.X, the data folders recipe/, loot_table/, advancement/, structure/, tags/item and tags/block -> recipes/, loot_tables/, advancements/, structures/, tags/items and tags/blocks, neoforge:conditions -> conditions with forge: condition types, result 'id' -> 'item', and c: tags -> forge: tags by the table in tags-forge) and applies it with git apply --3way. Conflicts are solved by hand. The 1.20.4 port commit 63fbbb33 is the reference for every reverse mapping, because the 1.20.1 base is its parent. Generated output under src/generated is never patched from upstream: it is rewritten by hand byte for byte as the 1.20.1 providers write it.
Upstream commits: none (local).
Files (on the base or new): nothing in the fork (process step).
Translation: Run the script with python -I from the scratchpad, never from inside the upstream clone.
Savegame: none.

Test: Apply 350da9b2 and 87f753a1 through the pipeline as a dry run, both apply after the import rewrite.

[config-port, 3 h] Port CommonConfig of main (34 keys) over the 1.20.1 one (24 keys). New keys: doBatDrops, farmerConfigurator, fluidLaserTransferRate, generateQuartz, generateCanola, generateCoffee, generateFlax, generateRice, leafGeneratorArea, leafGeneratorCooldown, leafGeneratorCPPerLeaf. Use main's camelCase names from the start (1be720f6 renamed keys with spaces and warns that list configs reset). The base was never released, so no shipped actuallyadditions-common.toml exists to migrate. hideEnergyOverlay goes into a new ClientConfig (9c6859cd, 12527cd1): the base registers only the COMMON config (ActuallyAdditions constructor), so register ModConfig.Type.CLIENT inside the existing DistExecutor client branch. Drop the base's furDropChance and 'Drill Extra Whitelist' only if nothing reads them, else keep them. e22b1615 fixes config spam (values read during load).
Upstream commits: e22b1615, 1be720f6, 9c6859cd, 12527cd1, e21713e3, a831cbbd, 5182ac8b, 16cd3a69, 2ffe78d6, b9435301, b66af844, 1f78ecc5, 8d01e07d.
Files (on the base or new): mod/config/CommonConfig.java, mod/config/ClientConfig.java, mod/ActuallyAdditions.java.
Translation: ModConfigSpec -> ForgeConfigSpec. a831cbbd (built in config screen) is not ported (see the exclusion neoforge-config-screen), so its lang keys are not added. Read values lazily, never in static initialisers or Item.Properties (IllegalStateException before load).

Test: First boot writes actuallyadditions-common.toml and, on the client, actuallyadditions-client.toml with all keys, no WARN about config spam, values change behaviour after a restart. The server config of the pack lives in config/ and is edited only while the java process is gone.

[datagen-provider-fixes, 4 h] First run runData on the untouched base (build.gradle:48-57 already has the data run) and record, without committing, how its output differs from the committed src/generated (335 models, 120 blockstates, 109 recipes): the base is a work in progress snapshot, so its committed files may already disagree with its own providers, and every later hand written file must match the providers as they stand after this feature, not the stale committed files. Then port: bucket item models (ead1d9be), advancement generation (50407e95), item models for all items (48766771, 19afc5f0, closes the UPSTREAM.md gaps 'booklet and crate_keeper have no item model'), cutout render type on every crop stage model instead of skipping the first (93242df1), recipe generator lookup (b70c7916), crushing recipe datagen (c1b23b52, the source of 1.3.21 'Fix invalid Crushing recipes'). Every provider change is mirrored by hand in src/generated byte for byte, the ship stage reruns runData and reconciles.
Upstream commits: ead1d9be, 50407e95, 4a16be41 (generated part), dcc2220a, 19afc5f0, 48766771, b70c7916, 93242df1, 556f4a77, a706f37b, c1b23b52, a7e2d627, 88b0775f.

Recipe JSON: result 'id' -> 'item', neoforge:conditions -> conditions with forge:mod_loaded, ingredient lists unchanged. The 1.20.4 generated files (branch 1.20.4) are the closest template for 1.20.1 output, they still use the plural folder names and 'item' keys.

[baseline-boot-smoke, 3 h] Boot the base alone on Forge 47.4.18 (client and dedicated server) and in the full pack on Arclight, and fix only what stops the boot. Of the cited upstream commits only f9897f06 applies: ActuallyAdditionsClient.java:97 registers ClientRegistryHandler, whose two @SubscribeEvent methods take mod bus events (ModelEvent.RegisterGeometryLoaders and BakingCompleted), on MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS. Move it to the mod bus or delete the empty class (its comment names a Tinkers' Construct excerpt, so deleting also drops that attribution need). Not needed on the base: 9ec20f48 (the base already registers the particle providers inside RegisterParticleProvidersEvent, ActuallyAdditions.java:117 and 158-160) and 758001e2 (a 1.21 regression, the base wraps the client listeners in DistExecutor at ActuallyAdditions.java:114). The base registers the fully commented DungeonLoot on the Forge bus (ActuallyAdditions.java:105), which is harmless on Forge 47 and goes with loot-modifiers (4a16be41). OLD jar of the savegame test: the task defines it as the build of the vendored base, which the setup stage recorded (SHA-1 c37140ce, copy in the scratchpad base-jar folder). If that jar boots clean, it stays the OLD jar. If the base needs boot fixes, the OLD jar is the base plus only those fixes, and its SHA-1 replaces c37140ce in the savegame test notes.
Upstream commits: f9897f06 (9ec20f48 and 758001e2 checked, not needed).
Files (on the base or new): mod/ActuallyAdditions.java, mod/ActuallyAdditionsClient.java, mod/ClientRegistryHandler.java.

bundles.name: aa-server-safety
bundles.title: Dedicated server and multiplayer safety: client class split, packet validation, menu validity and the drill upgrade dupe, player data sync
bundles.spec:
[dedicated-server-client-split, 8 h] On the base, BlockPhantom, BlockLaserRelay, BlockAtomicReconstructor, BlockPlayerInterface, BlockVerticalDigger, BlockLavaFactoryController and ItemBooklet implement IHudDisplay with a displayHud(GuiGraphics, Minecraft, ...) method, the laser relay tiles import net.minecraft.client.resources.language.I18n and build their mode strings with I18n.get, and PacketHandler holds the client handlers that call Minecraft.getInstance(). Also live and touched by the split: ItemCoffee.MilkIngredient.getExtraText calls I18n.get in a common method (ItemCoffee.java:161, replaced by coffee-machine-and-coffee), util/StringUtil and util/AssetUtil mix client methods into common utility classes, UpdateChecker (only its @OnlyIn onTick touches client code, fine). 668f7ffe moves the HUDs into IBlockHud plus client only classes (LaserRelayHud, LavaFactoryControllerHud, MinerHud, PhantomHud, later FarmerHud) registered from ClientEvents. 844efe42 moves the goggles client tick and the client packet handlers out of common classes. 0226078a, 3a767e18 and d64b530f replace I18n with Component.translatable in common code. a20c25eb guards the Patchouli page registration. Upstream ties this to dedicated server crashes with Lithium (#1434). The same verifier class loading hits Arclight's dedicated server when a common class merges a client type in a stack map frame. Curios calls (ItemCrafterOnAStick in main imports CuriosApi in the common item) go into a separate compat class that only runs when ModList says curios is loaded.
Upstream commits: 668f7ffe, 844efe42, 8fd9afe8, 0226078a, d1ceffca, 3a767e18, d64b530f, a20c25eb.
Files (on the base or new): mod/blocks/IHudDisplay.java, mod/blocks/IBlockHud.java, mod/blocks/blockhuds/, mod/items/ItemEngineerGoggles.java, mod/network/PacketHandler.java, mod/network/PacketHandlerClient.java, mod/event/ClientEvents.java, mod/tile/TileEntityLaserRelay*.java, mod/util/StringUtil.java, mod/util/AssetUtil.java.
Translation: The 1.21 PacketHandlerClient and ClientPayloadHandler become a client only class called through DistExecutor.unsafeRunWhenOn(Dist.CLIENT) from the SimpleChannel consumer. Keep @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) off interfaces that common classes implement. RegisterGuiOverlaysEvent or RenderGuiOverlayEvent drives the HUDs on 1.20.1.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: javap -c over every class outside the client packages of the built jar: no net/minecraft/client reference outside methods that carry @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) or classes only reached through DistExecutor. Dedicated Arclight server: place, wrench and right click every AA block, use every AA item, no NoClassDefFoundError and no 'invalid dist' crash.

[packet-hardening, 6.5 h] Local deviation, upstream main still trusts the client (ServerPayloadHandler.handleButtonToTile and siblings read dimension, pos and playerId from the packet). On the base (PacketHandler.java:92-171) GUI_BUTTON_TO_TILE, GUI_NUMBER_TO_TILE, GUI_STRING_TO_TILE and GUI_BUTTON_TO_CONTAINER take WorldID, X, Y, Z and PlayerID from the packet: any client can press buttons on any AA machine in any dimension as any player, load chunks through getBlockEntity, throw a NullPointerException with an unknown WorldID and a ClassCastException when PlayerID names a non player. PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER edits the player data of any UUID. Second hole: DATA_HANDLERS is one list for both directions (PacketHandler.java:195-203) and PacketClientToServer.fromBytes accepts any index (PacketClientToServer.java:39), so a client can send the index of a client handler (LASER_HANDLER, TILE_ENTITY_HANDLER, SYNC_PLAYER_DATA, LASER_PARTICLE_HANDLER). On the dedicated server their handleData carries @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) and is stripped, so the call throws AbstractMethodError, and on a LAN host it runs client code with the guest's NBT (TILE_ENTITY_HANDLER feeds readSyncableNBT of the host's client level). Fix: (1) a serverbound allow list (the four GUI handlers, PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER, and the later hotkey and item tag handlers) checked in PacketClientToServer, a clientbound allow list in PacketServerToClient. (2) The sender (context.getSender()) is the only player, the dimension must be the sender's level, the position must be loaded (hasChunkAt) and within 8 blocks (64 square) or belong to the menu the sender has open, PlayerID and WorldID are ignored. (3) PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER: after c8e90aef its only effect is setDirty (main ServerPayloadHandler.handleSyncPlayer has every type branch commented out), so it becomes a no op that keeps its index. (4) Each reactor clamps its own values: firework box ranges (firework-box), XP solidifier buttonID lower bound (xp-solidifier), button ids of the digger, ranged collector and sack menus. (5) Exceptions inside enqueueWork vanish in the CompletableFuture today: add exceptionally() with a WARN line naming the player (main disconnects the player instead). Bump PROTOCOL_VERSION from 4 to 5 once, here. Later bundles of this backport append handlers (hotkey, item tag) without another bump because no build ships in between.
Upstream commits: 9d166ac9 (only its split of client and server handlers).
Files (on the base or new): mod/network/PacketHandler.java, mod/network/PacketClientToServer.java, mod/network/PacketServerToClient.java, mod/network/PacketHelperServer.java.
Translation: Keep the SimpleChannel actuallyadditions:main and the NBT carrying PacketClientToServer format, so the client side code does not change shape. 9d166ac9 (1.21 networking overhaul into typed payloads) is not ported as such.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: A dev only client command in a separate source set that the jar does not contain (KubeJS cannot send AA serverbound packets) sends crafted packets: a button press on a machine 20 blocks away, one in another dimension, a foreign PlayerID, an unknown WorldID, the index of each client handler and a PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER with another UUID. None has an effect, the server logs one WARN each and keeps running. A stock 1.1.52 client gets a clean protocol mismatch disconnect.

[menu-open-and-validity, 2 h] Both cited commits are already in effect on the base: f2596f97 feeds the block position into openMenu, which the base already does through NetworkHooks.openScreen(player, tile, pos) (BlockContainerBase.java:55 and the oil generator, coffee machine, canola press and fermenting barrel blocks), and 82aaacf1 only replaces worldPosition by getBlockPos() in canPlayerUse, which returns the same field. The real work is local: ContainerDrill, ContainerFilter and ContainerFireworkBox return true from stillValid. Drill upgrade dupe: ContainerDrill reads the upgrades from inventory.getSelected() at open and writes them back to inventory.getSelected() in removed() (ContainerDrill.java:130-136, unchanged on main). A client that sends a ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket while the menu is open changes the selected slot, so on close the remaining upgrades are written into a second drill while the first keeps its old NBT with every upgrade the player took out. Fix: remember the slot index and the ItemStack at open, stillValid returns false once the selected index or the stack identity changed, removed() writes only into that remembered stack. The same pattern for ContainerFilter (ghost items, no dupe, but it overwrites the wrong stack). ContainerFireworkBox uses canPlayerUse. The existing SlotImmovable and the SWAP check (ContainerDrill.java:57-61, 121-127) stay.
Upstream commits: f2596f97, 82aaacf1 (both checked, no change needed).
Files (on the base or new): mod/inventory/ContainerDrill.java, mod/inventory/ContainerFilter.java, mod/inventory/ContainerFireworkBox.java.
Translation: None.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: Every machine screen opens on a dedicated server and closes when the player walks 9 blocks away. With the dev client command, open the drill screen, take an upgrade out, switch the selected slot to a second drill by packet: the screen closes and no second drill gains upgrades.

[player-and-world-data, 2 h] A crash when client code asks for player data (2a4e9666 hands the client a local PlayerSave instead of casting to ServerLevel), and c8e90aef drops the old booklet bookmark and trial data from PlayerData. Also a base bug: SYNC_PLAYER_DATA is a clientbound handler that reads context.getSender() (PacketHandler.java:134), which is null for clientbound packets, so the client never receives its player data (bat wings state) and logs an ERROR each time. Use Minecraft.getInstance().player in the client handler class of dedicated-server-client-split (main ClientPayloadHandler.handleSyncPlayer uses the context player of the clientbound flow). Keep reading the old keys so an OLD world loads, stop writing them.
Upstream commits: 2a4e9666, c8e90aef.
Files (on the base or new): mod/data/WorldData.java, mod/data/PlayerData.java, mod/network/PacketHandlerClient.java.
Translation: SavedData load and save without HolderLookup.
Savegame: WorldData keys Networks and PlayerData unchanged, booklet keys (Bookmarks, Trials, DidTutorial) stop being written. PlayerSave keeps BookGotten, HasBatWings, BatWingsFlyTime and ShouldDisableWings.
New ids: none.
Test: Savegame test: an OLD world with laser networks and player data loads, networks still work. On a dedicated server the client gets its player data on join without the ERROR 'Tried to receive Player Data for the current player'.

bundles.title: Recipes, forge: tags with the c: map, advancements and the JEI plugin shell
bundles.spec:
[recipes-completion, 12 h] The base has 109 generated recipe files and many WIP items without a recipe, main has 204. Port the generator changes: crystal block compress and decompress (8f73813a), missing recipes and lang (1e323010), the black quartz block family (e8df077d), smelting and blasting of black quartz ore (d1f77f3d), rice dough to bread (c29830ad), rice paper (cf80d174), conflicts (f524eccc, fc63fa00 #1465), correct amounts for walls, slabs and stairs plus stonecutter recipes (d0f8c24a, changelog 1.3.11), smooth black quartz (40012ae3 PR #1501) and the machine recipes listed in their own features. Walk main's recipe folder file by file against the base and write the 1.20.1 form of each missing file by hand, generator first. Conditions translate one to one: neoforge:mod_loaded -> forge:mod_loaded, neoforge:not plus neoforge:tag_empty (coffee_ingredient/milk_tagged.json) -> forge:not plus forge:tag_empty (both exist in Forge 47, TagEmptyCondition). Forge 47 evaluates the top level 'conditions' key for every recipe type, so AA's own serializers need no condition code.
Upstream commits: 2040c68e, 8f73813a, 1e323010, a622e497, 06ef7146, e8df077d, d1f77f3d, c29830ad, cf80d174, f524eccc, fc63fa00, d0f8c24a, 40012ae3, 1440baa4, 9492973a, cad57217, 7c7a095c, 8abfa241, b69847d1, 5a921e10, 3f356896, b68cfecd, 9d76fad7.
Files (on the base or new): data/ItemRecipeGenerator.java, data/BlockRecipeGenerator.java, src/generated/resources/data/actuallyadditions/recipes/.
Translation: Folder recipes/, result {'item':..., 'count':...}, ingredients with forge: tags by the table in tags-forge, conditions with forge: types. The 1.20.4 generated tree is the template.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: All recipes load (no 'Parsing error loading recipe' in the log), JEI or EMI shows a recipe for every AA item except the intentionally uncraftable ones, AlmostUnified reports no AA recipe it cannot read.

[tags-forge, 4 h] The base ships no forge: tag at all (src/generated has only minecraft mineable, walls, needs_stone_tool and damage type tags plus six actuallyadditions tags). Port ActuallyTags and the generators of main with c: mapped to forge:. Tags to add: forge:gems/black_quartz, forge:ores/black_quartz, forge:storage_blocks/black_quartz and the twelve crystal and empowered crystal storage blocks (#1418), forge:ores, forge:ores_in_ground/stone, forge:seeds/rice, coffee, canola, flax and forge:seeds, forge:crops/rice, coffee, canola, flax and forge:crops, forge:slimeballs for the rice slimeball (main uses c:slime_balls and c:slimeballs), minecraft:crops block tag for the AA crops (9689b4c1), the AIOT tool tags, actuallyadditions:stone_ore_replaceables and deepslate_ore_replaceables, actuallyadditions:lamps. The c: to forge: table for every tag main's data names (grep of main src/generated and src/main/resources): c:cobblestones -> forge:cobblestone, c:stones -> forge:stone, c:obsidians -> forge:obsidian, c:glass_blocks -> forge:glass, c:sands -> forge:sand, c:strings -> forge:string, c:leathers -> forge:leather, c:gunpowders -> forge:gunpowder, c:slime_balls and c:slimeballs -> forge:slimeballs, c:ender_pearls -> forge:ender_pearls, c:rods/wooden -> forge:rods/wooden, c:chests/wooden -> forge:chests/wooden, c:seeds -> forge:seeds, c:milk -> forge:milk (item tag, guarded by forge:tag_empty), c:dyes/<color> -> forge:dyes/<color>, c:dusts/redstone and glowstone -> forge:dusts/..., c:ingots/iron and gold, c:gems/diamond, emerald, lapis and quartz, c:storage_blocks/redstone, lapis, iron, emerald, diamond and coal -> the same path under forge:, c:ore_bearing_ground/netherrack -> forge:ore_bearing_ground/netherrack, c:ores -> forge:ores, biome tags c:is_overworld -> minecraft:is_overworld, c:is_hot/overworld -> forge:is_hot/overworld, c:is_cold/overworld -> forge:is_cold/overworld, c:is_sparse_vegetation/overworld -> forge:is_sparse/overworld, c:is_dense_vegetation/overworld -> forge:is_dense/overworld. c:bucket/canola_oil and its three siblings have no forge: standard: keep them as actuallyadditions:buckets/<fluid> unless a pack recipe needs them.
Upstream commits: 1d581fc1, c952c779, 9689b4c1, af8f1f18, e37019a5, 8d56947d, e3dd3290, 4789e61e.
Files (on the base or new): api/ActuallyTags.java, data/BlockTagsGenerator.java, data/ItemTagsGenerator.java.
Translation: AlmostUnified 0.11.0 (config/almostunified/unify.json) lists neither black_quartz nor any crystal in materials, so tagging them unifies nothing. Local fix: an AAFakePlayers helper around FakePlayerFactory.get(serverLevel, PROFILE) with a fixed GameProfile ([ActuallyAdditions], a constant UUID). Forge 47 caches one such player per level and profile, installs its FakePlayerNetHandler (FakePlayer.java:85) and drops it in unloadLevel, so the helper keeps no strong reference across a level unload. Each use positions the player at the machine and clears its hands afterwards. Every break goes through fireFakeHarvestEventsForDropChance (posts BlockEvent.BreakEvent, honours cancellation, then ForgeEventFactory.doPlayerHarvestCheck). Every lens placement or conversion posts ForgeEventFactory.onBlockPlace(fakePlayer, BlockSnapshot, Direction) and reverts on cancel. Phantom Breaker drops use boundPosition and the target's block entity. bb06b24a adds the playerWillDestroy call to WorldUtil.breakExtraBlock (the drill's area mining, changelog 1.3.11 'drill not dropping block contents for certain mods'), which needs the drills bundle merged first.

Translation: Arclight 1.0.6 (safeiter2 jar, javap on the extracted mod_file) bridges both Forge events: BlockBreakEventDispatcher.onBreakBlock turns every posted BlockEvent.BreakEvent into a Bukkit BlockBreakEvent with the fake player's CraftPlayer and copies the cancel flag back, BlockPlaceEventDispatcher.onBlockPlace does the same for BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent when the entity is a ServerPlayer (FakePlayer is one). The Placer and Phantom Placer already use fake.gameMode.useItemOn, which reaches Arclight's BlockItemMixin and fires BlockPlaceEvent. ForgeHooks.onBlockBreakEvent (Drill area mining, WorldUtil.breakExtraBlock) posts the same Forge event. NeoForge EventHooks.doPlayerHarvestCheck(player, state, level, pos) becomes Forge 47 ForgeEventFactory.doPlayerHarvestCheck(player, state, state.canHarvestBlock(level, pos, player)). With one fixed profile a claim plugin has to trust [ActuallyAdditions] for machines to work inside claims. The pack runs EssentialsX only, and per owner fake players would need a new additive owner key on every tile, which stays out of scope and goes on the open items list.

New local findings:
- Packet handlers: DATA_HANDLERS serves both directions. A client can send the index of a client only handler, which hits a stripped @OnlyIn method on the dedicated server and runs client code on a LAN host. The firework box stores raw slider numbers (clamp to main's GUI ranges). The XP solidifier lacks a lower bound on the button id. PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER is a no-op after c8e90aef. Exceptions in enqueueWork are swallowed silently. KubeJS cannot inject serverbound packets, so the test uses a dev only client command.
- Drill upgrade dupe: ContainerDrill writes the upgrades to whatever hotbar slot is selected at close (ContainerDrill.java:130-136). A client that changes the selected slot by packet duplicates them. Fixed in menu-open-and-validity.
- SYNC_PLAYER_DATA uses context.getSender() on the client, which is always null, so player data never syncs.
- Vertical digger: the base sentinel -1/0 breaks below Y 0. Main's 738f098b resets every digger at each chunk load. Use an additive marker key instead.
- 38d6404b adds a block state property persistent to all crops (additive, needs blockstate variants). The savegame note was missing.
